newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-SAUNDERS GETS FIRST WIN, HOMER AS MARLINS BEAT BRAVES.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-SAUNDERS GETS FIRST WIN, HOMER AS MARLINS BEAT BRAVES.

text.p: Tony Saunders allowed four hits over six scoreless innings for his first major-league win and hit his first major-league home run Thursday to lead the Florida Marlins to a 5-1 victory over the Atlanta Braves.

Saunders (1-1) walked four and struck out four in his fifth career start. He was hitless in the first seven at-bats of his young career before leading off the third by driving a 1-2 pitch from last year's Cy Young winner, Tom Glavine, over the right-field fence. That gave the Marlins a 1-0 lead.
"Once it was out, I was surprised," Saunders said. "It hasn't hit me what I've done tonight. I lowered my head and ran around the bases. I didn't want to show him up."

"I wasn't even trying to throw a strike. I don't know what happened," said Glavine (4-2), who allowed five runs and six hits in four innings and left after he was struck on the left hand by Saunders' pitch in the fifth inning.
X-rays on Glavine's hand were negative and he is not expected to miss a start.
"When I hit him I felt terrible," said Saunders.
"It put a damper on my evening. It's something I'll never forget. I called over there and told him how badly I felt. He said 'It hurt more giving up the home run to you than getting hit by you.'
"He told me not to worry about it. Pitching against him is amazing to me. I've been watching him pitch for a number of years."
"I consider myself lucky I got out quick so it didn't hit me square," said Glavine. "Right now my index finger is a little numb. We'll see what happens tomorrow.
"Pitchers don't like seeing other pitchers get hurt, especially if they've had something to do with it. But it's all forgotten, I will harbour no ill feelings."
In Colorado, Jason Kendall's three-run double capped an eight-run fourth inning as the Pittsburgh Pirates outslugged the Rockies 10-8 for their sixth win in eight games.

Pittsburgh trailed 5-1 entering the inning before Kevin Elster led off with his sixth homer to ignite the outburst. The Pirates sent 12 batters to the plate and had six hits in their biggest inning of the year. Elster had two RBI and scored twice in the inning.
Mark Johnson had three hits and Al Martin added a solo homer for the Pirates, who scored 24 runs in sweeping the two-game series at Colorado.
Esteban Loaiza improved to 4-0 despite allowing six runs and 11 hits in 5 2/3 innings. Rich Loiselle, the fifth Pirates pitcher, worked the ninth for his second save.
Jamey Wright (4-2) was pounded for nine runs and eight hits -- including two homers -- in 3 2/3 innings. Colorado pitching has allowed 35 runs in its last three games.
In St Louis, Gary Gaetti's three-run double highlighted a four-run sixth inning and Andy Benes pitched eight strong innings as the Cardinals beat the Philadelphia Phillies 6-2.
Benes (2-1) allowed two runs and five hits and struck out five in eight innings.

The Cardinals, who recorded their eighth win in their last nine home games and their ninth victory in their last 12 games overall, scored five runs off loser Mike Mimbs (0-3) after being held in check by Phillies starter Matt Beech for the first four innings.
Mimbs replaced Beech in the fifth and allowed Mike Difelice's first major league home run, a game-tying, solo shot. Mimbs was tagged for four more runs in the sixth.
In Houston, Mike Hampton won for the first time in seven starts and Derek Bell homered and drove in a pair of runs as the Astros defeated the New York Mets, 4-2.
Hampton (2-3) won for the first time since defeating the Braves on the second day of the season. He allowed two runs and seven hits over seven innings with five strikeouts.

He walked just one and did not throw more than two balls to a batter until Butch Huskey was issued a free pass leading off the sixth. The southpaw's control was so effective that he threw 17 straight strikes during one span from the third through fifth innings.
In San Diego, Terry Mulholland allowed two runs over 6 2/3 innings and Brian McRae and Jose Hernandez hit solo homers as the Chicago Cubs defeated the slumping Padres 6-2.
Sammy Sosa went 4-for-5 for the Cubs, who have split their last 18 games since an 0-14 start. Mulholland (3-3) gave up six hits, did not walk a batter and struck out three.
Fernando Valenzuela (1-4) suffered the loss, getting tagged for five runs and 10 hits in five innings. San Diego has not won consecutive games since April 11-13 and has lost 12 of its last 15 games.
